claims.text: The starting AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy has a uniform, fine lamellar state.
Adding a controlled amount of carbon nanotubes can increase the alloy's strength.
Adding a controlled amount of carbon nanotubes can increase the alloy's plasticity.
Adding carbon nanotubes can improve resistance to extreme temperature fluctuations.
Adding carbon nanotubes can improve resistance to long-term mechanical loading.
Adding carbon nanotubes can improve room-temperature creep resistance.
Adding carbon nanotubes can improve resistance to corrosive conditions.
Carbon nanotubes reinforce the alloy matrix.
CNT–alloy matrix interactions enhance the alloy's mechanical properties.
A protective CNT network improves corrosion resistance.
The proposed performance improvement applies from -200 °C to 800 °C.
The proposed performance improvement applies under mechanical loading up to 1000 MPa.
The proposed performance improvement applies during corrosive exposure lasting up to 1000 hours.
The baseline for comparison is as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The experiment will compare CNT-modified material with the baseline using tensile strength, elongation at break, creep resistance, and corrosion rate.
The hypothesis is declared falsified if the CNT-modified alloy fails to improve at least two measured properties by 10% or more relative to the baseline.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts improvement in strength, plasticity, thermal-fluctuation resistance, long-term-loading resistance, creep resistance, and corrosion resistance, but the falsification rule permits the hypothesis to survive when only two measured properties improve. It therefore does not decisively test the full multi-property prediction.
